title: Calculating Optical Density Using MCID
author: Andrea Vogel

steps.title: Create workspace folder
steps.instruction: If this is the first time, create a folder named “Your Name” on the desktop to store all MCiD files.

steps.title: Launch and size MCiD
steps.instruction: Open MCiD by double‑clicking its desktop icon and stretch the program window to fill both screens so the picture occupies one whole screen.

steps.title: Set display format
steps.instruction: In MCiD go to Settings → Display Format, select Mono (12 bit), and click OK.

steps.title: Select camera input and verify
steps.instruction: Choose Settings → Input Selection → QICAM – 12 Lightbox Camera and click OK. Verify that the light‑box camera’s blue and green LEDs are on (switch on top of camera) and that the color camera on the other scope is also on (they are daisy‑chained).

steps.title: Adjust magnification and focus
steps.instruction: Press the Digitize button (camera icon). Use ink on a test film to check focus; if out of focus, adjust the camera arm crank while the Digitize dialog is open, then click OK to capture an image.

steps.title: Prepare flat‑field correction
steps.instruction: Remove the film from the lightbox. Change the pseudocolor bar on the top menu to SPECT2VIS. Turn the light‑box intensity knob until the blank field appears bluish‑pink (≈ 1000 lumens).

substeps.instruction: Ctrl‑click the Digitize icon and choose Flat Field Correction.
If a previous flat field exists, click “Clear”.

steps.title: Acquire flat‑field correction
steps.instruction: Click “Acquire” to generate a new flat‑field correction. Ensure the following settings (do not change them): Correction source = Digitize; Correction method = Pixel by pixel; Frame average = 4; enable both Smoothing and Median filters; then click OK.

steps.title: Set up density calibration
steps.instruction: Place the film back on the lightbox and view the standards slide. Open Operations (left menu) → Calibration ROD – relative optical density.

steps.title: Enter density standards
steps.instruction: From the top menu choose Calibrations → Density, then select “Cal Stds”. Input standard values from lowest to highest (zero first). If no calibration table exists, click “None” and create one. Enter numbers from the data sheet into the “Standards unit” column (calculate each entry as nCi/mg × decay rate). Click in the “Value Read” column next to the first standard, then digitize each standard, starting with a zero reading from plain film and proceeding from lightest to darkest.

steps.title: Generate calibration curve
steps.instruction: In the curve‑type dialog choose cubic spline (smoothed) or the curve that best fits the data by eye. Enable extrapolation for both minimum and maximum values so the software can interpret data outside the standard range.

steps.title: Perform sample measurements
steps.instruction: Open an Excel spreadsheet on a nearby laptop (do not use the MCiD spreadsheet). Choose unilateral measurement (usual choice). For the VP region select an oval shape (Ctrl‑drag to resize, Alt‑drag to rotate; Ctrl‑click the shape menu to record measurements; F4 clears the image but not data). Click the region of interest and then the background (two clicks) to obtain data; use F4 to clear and repeat if numbers differ. Red numbers are extrapolated from the standards.

substeps.instruction: When all measurements for an animal are complete, clear the sheet data by clicking “Clear”.

steps.title: Shut down and clean
steps.instruction: Turn off the camera on the microscope and cover the scope. Turn off the camera on the lightbox. Wipe the lightbox with Sparkle and Kimwipes, then place the blue lab‑bench sheet on the lightbox with the soft side down.
